cases.name: holdout3-document-review-access-review-policy
cases.promptMarkdown:
Use the `siang:document-review` skill (Skill tool, `skill: "siang:document-review"`) to check our user access review policy, `policy.md`, against the internal control it has to satisfy, `control-standard.md`, before the auditors see it. Review only: leave `policy.md` unchanged. Put your findings ledger in `findings.md`, one row or entry per finding with the policy location (section or step), the problem, and the control clause (AC-07.x) it relates to, if any. Do not list things that are fine.

Your final message is one line giving the number of findings, nothing else.

If the Skill tool reports the skill as unknown or unavailable, do the same task yourself and still end with the final message described above.

cases.name: holdout3-document-review-backup-runbook
cases.promptMarkdown:
Use the `siang:document-review` skill (Skill tool, `skill: "siang:document-review"`) to audit `runbook.md`, our restore runbook for the orders database, against our runbook standard in `runbook-standard.md`. This is a review only: do not edit `runbook.md`. Write a findings ledger to `review.md`: one entry per finding, each with its location in the runbook (section or step number), what is wrong, and which rule of the standard it breaks, if any. Only report real problems.

Your final message is one line giving the number of findings, nothing else.

If the Skill tool reports the skill as unknown or unavailable, do the same task yourself and still end with the final message described above.

cases.name: holdout3-technical-writing-report-export
cases.promptMarkdown:
Use the `siang:technical-writing` skill (Skill tool, `skill: "siang:technical-writing"`) on `docs/exporting.md`. It is a how-to someone drafted months ago for exporting our event log with `report.py`, and support keeps getting tickets from people who followed it. Rewrite `docs/exporting.md` as a how-to that takes an analyst from a fresh checkout to an export file they can open: what they need first, the command, the options and their defaults, and where the file ends up. Base every fact on `report.py` and `report.toml` as they are now; do not edit either file.

Your final message is one line naming the most harmful mistake in the old draft, nothing else.

If the Skill tool reports the skill as unknown or unavailable, do the same task yourself and still end with the final message described above.

cases.name: holdout3-technical-writing-snap-backup
cases.promptMarkdown:
Use the `siang:technical-writing` skill (Skill tool, `skill: "siang:technical-writing"`) to fix `README.md`. It documents `bin/snap`, our directory backup script, but it was written for an older version and a new teammate could not get a backup to work from it. Rewrite `README.md` so someone who has never seen the script can take their first backup and knows which options exist and what they default to. Everything in it must match `bin/snap` and `snap.conf` as they are now. Do not change the script or the config.

Your final message is one line saying what was wrong in the old README, nothing else.

If the Skill tool reports the skill as unknown or unavailable, do the same task yourself and still end with the final message described above.
